page: The UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, along with 50 GB of local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the processor in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance and large-block memory bandwidth read/write speeds fall into the average range. Conversely, PassMark CPU and memory scores, Geekbench multi-core results, and Redis SET operations are positioned in the bottom 25% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is particularly constrained, registering in the bottom 10%.

Due to its shared CPU allocation, this instance exhibits a high resource density that offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring significant memory capacity relative to compute power. However, the shared CPU model introduces performance variability under sustained multi-threaded loads, as evidenced by the lower multi-core benchmark tiers. This server is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads, such as lightweight databases, caching layers, static web serving, and basic text or image processing tasks that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance.

It is well-suited for lightweight database operations, static web serving, caching, and general-purpose development environments.
